reasoning_traces.think:
The factorized attention transformer enables real-time coverage classification by decomposing spatio-temporal player tensors into spatial and temporal components. Spatial attention captures immediate player interactions—such as receiver-defender proximity—while temporal attention encodes motion history. This dual structure allows for accurate prediction of defensive shells and targeted defender assignments. In contrast, the hierarchical Bayesian model addresses uncertainty in small samples by borrowing strength across similar players and roles. It uses partial pooling to stabilize estimates, particularly useful when evaluating emerging talents or underperforming veterans. The regime mixture model introduces dynamic weighting of features based on situational context, such as score differential or down-and-distance. These three primitives form a layered reasoning pipeline: first, attention identifies key interactions; second, Bayesian inference stabilizes estimates; third, regime mixing adjusts for contextual variability. Together they resolve the failure modes observed in Week 6, where naive models misjudged pass outcomes due to ignoring coverage persistence and player-specific regression effects.
